key_risks: Rapid Hormuz de-escalation or shipping normalization could reverse oil and energy gains sharply
Hawkish July 29 FOMC or sticky July CPI (driven by energy) could pressure risk assets and financials
High-volatility biotech and oil positions amplify drawdowns if risk appetite fades on soft growth data
Profit-taking after strong bank results or sector rotation away from recent winners

portfolio.rationale: Hormuz blockade reimposed and rising oil prices (Brent/WTI multi-week highs) support energy equities over the one-month window amid unresolved shipping and military risks.
Direct crude exposure benefits from the same Strait of Hormuz supply disruption premium and recent price strength into the scoring window.
Record Q2 bank profits, strong markets revenue (especially equities), and rising consumer spending provide near-term earnings momentum.
Strong 30-day relative performance and risk-on biotech momentum can continue if soft labor data supports risk appetite before August data.
Recent outperformance and thematic demand provide diversification with lower direct oil/geopolitical beta than pure energy.

portfolio_rationale: Concentrate in energy/oil for the active Hormuz supply risk premium while adding financials on confirmed strong bank results and selective high-momentum equities (biotech, cyber) for alpha versus SPY over the one-month close-to-close window.
rationale_summary: Geopolitical oil upside plus bank earnings strength and recent factor/sector momentum are the highest-conviction near-term drivers before the August 14 exit; avoid duration and pure growth given sticky energy inflation and Fed stance.
